asked.question: A cycle of a single-agent run has ended: does the agent get another?

options.summary: another cycle, with the run's continue message
options.consequences: a further cycle's time and tokens
the session keeps what it did and nothing further is started

decision.rationale: All three parts of the brief are implemented and committed, with evidence. Part 1: one writer (lib/src/proof_wire.rs) and one reader (lib/python/jvmcontract_io.py) for proof output, with ordinary ingestion, live and archived selectors, the benchmark and the solver comparison all switched to it, and helper decisions as data. Part 2: one class selection (ClassPath::bind), checked against what the JVM loads at launch. Part 3: array induction as a library method; the five contracts repeat their stored results and the negative control stays unresolved (the job passed on a real solver run). The reproducer tables are kept as tests. All 58 archived selector records validate the same, and none of the 2,933 published benchmark and solver records changes score. All that is left for the agent is the proof-tier job (about 45 minutes), so by the skill's rule I stop rather than have it wait in a cycle. I'll watch the queue and restart the run only if that job fails. Pinning a new benchmark baseline is the user's decision, as the report says.

confidence.basis: the loop's event 2 (single-lib-architecture-fast-follow/events.jsonl), the example's state and the verification queue

recovery.undo: start the run again (single_run.py start NAME): it continues the same session
